how: Made by hand, after the campaign, from the Linux host's window log, its backup job's log and this project's session records, with each time in UTC. The host does not record logins: its login record was last written before the campaign began, so each login's time is the session records', known to the minute. A query phase with no query named is the whole phase of that kind for the variant, since the documents keep no time per query. The other project's watcher's logins were added on 2026-11-17 from its status file and its period, mapped onto the phases by the run records' own times: a login its status file records is placed by that line, and one computed from the period between two recorded lines is given with its bounds as start and end. The capacity check's part is listed here, as the file it falls in was measured at this commit.

not_listed.what: the backup job's short routine runs, about ten seconds every fifteen minutes
not_listed.why: they ran through every timed step, so every phase may hold one, and the comparison documents keep no time per query or per write to place them; the kernel benchmark's file keeps no time per case, so only the run its attempt record ties to a case is listed

not_listed.what: a queued window request by this project, waiting from the slice's ArcticDB write on until the benchmark campaign took the window
not_listed.why: a waiting process whose processor use nothing records; it spans every phase from then on

not_listed.what: a queued window request by another project on the host during the benchmark campaign
not_listed.why: a waiting process whose processor use nothing records

not_listed.what: the refused attempts of the kernel benchmark and the fuzz step that was no result
not_listed.why: no committed file holds their figures

not_listed.what: another project's watcher's remote logins, about every half hour from 2026-11-14T15:22:16Z, each reading the host's window state and a few files
not_listed.why: those that fell in the refused attempts of the kernel benchmark (four) and in the fuzz step that was no result (one) touch no committed file; the rest are listed as entries, each recorded time from the watcher's status file and each computed time with its bounds

not_listed.what: the host's own scheduled jobs: a repository backup every fifteen minutes, a health collector and two small watchers every five minutes, two sync jobs every ten minutes, a file backup about hourly and daily maintenance
not_listed.why: they run through every window and were not stopped, as nothing on the host is changed for a measurement beyond the governor; the run records keep no list of them by phase apart from the events listed here, and what guards each timed figure is the per-CPU record of the other processors' use and the load rule
